claims.text: The initial material is a non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloy.
The as-deposited alloy has an ordered, single-phase hexagonal structure.
The initial alloy exhibits a sharp and hysteretic magnetocaloric response.
The initial alloy's sharp, hysteretic magnetocaloric response is caused by its bulk-processing history.
Reducing substrate temperature or sputtering power decreases grain size.
Reducing substrate temperature or sputtering power increases grain-boundary and interfacial-defect density.
Grain size and grain-boundary or interface density mediate nucleation and propagation of the magnetostructural transformation.
A finer-grained microstructure provides more nucleation sites for the magnetostructural transition.
Increasing the number of nucleation sites lowers the energy barrier for the first-order magnetostructural transition.
Lowering the transition barrier produces a smoother and more gradual phase transformation.
A smoother, more gradual transformation broadens the temperature range of the magnetocaloric entropy change.
A smoother, more gradual transformation reduces magnetocaloric hysteresis.
Greater interface area enhances magnetoelastic coupling and helps distribute transformation strain.
Microstructurally refined thin films will have a broader magnetocaloric entropy-change peak than the stated baseline.
Microstructurally refined thin films will have a smaller hysteresis width than the stated baseline under low applied fields.
The modified thin films will retain mechanical stability.
The modified thin films will enable rapid heat exchange.
Arc-melted ingots and melt-spun microribbons have larger grains than the proposed thin films.
Arc-melted ingots and melt-spun microribbons have a lower surface-to-volume ratio than the proposed thin films.
The predictions apply near the phase-transition temperature when composition is unchanged and an ordered single-phase hexagonal structure is retained.

contradictions.description: The initial state is called as-deposited, but its response is attributed to a bulk-processing history; the predicted outcome then identifies arc-melted ingots and melt-spun microribbons as the 'as-deposited baseline.' Bulk-processed products are not an as-deposited thin-film baseline.
The prediction is framed as a comparison with an as-deposited baseline, whereas the baseline field defines the comparator as bulk arc-melted ingots and melt-spun microribbons.
